doc.description:
A Rangefinder with I2C connection can be used as unidirectional rangefinder. Examples of devices are e.g. Maxbotix MB1240, GY-US42V2, Lightware SF11/C, SF20/C or SF30/C. The sensor can be used as a distance-measuring tool to detect the range (distance) to a surfaces. Usecase for example: AGL hold,terrain following or landing assist.
To be able to use the I2C version of a Rangefinder, add this module to your airframe and set needed parameters.
Notes: + The maximum useful detection distance is 4m for common rangefinder based small sized sensors, even if datasheet e.g. states 7m. For most I2C ultrasonic type of devices, a sampling rate of at least 15Hz is supported. However, if measurements are taken at longer distances, the time required for the ultrasonic pulse to return increases, which may limit the maximum achievable sampling rate. It is recommended to adjust the RANGEFINDER_I2C_PERIODIC_FREQUENCY parameter according to the sensor's capabilities and the expected measurement range to ensure reliable readings.
+ If the distance is read but the scale is incorrect, adjust the RANGEFINDER_I2C_SCALE parameter to match the sensor's specifications. The scale factor can also be determined experimentally by measuring a known distance and adjusting the scale until the output matches the expected value.
+ If the sensor is used in an airframe with landing gear, it is recommended to set the RANGEFINDER_I2C_OFFSET to the length of the landing gear, so that the AGL value is correct. Keep in mind that most ultrasonic type of sensors have a deadzone of 0.15m to 0.25m, so the AGL cannot be measured if landinggear shorter than the deadzone range.
+ There is an option to compensate the AGL value for body rotation, which is useful if e.g. a roll maneuver, the sensor is not pointing straight down it compensates the AGL value for the body rotation.
+ Also an option to filter the sensor output is available, which is useful if the sensor is noisy or has a lot of outliers, in case of a sonar type sensors, almost always the case. Lidar type of sensors are usually less noisy and have less outliers, so filtering better be disabled.
+ An option to set a different I2C address is available in some hardware but not implemented to set dynamically in this driver. Use external tools to change the I2C address if needed and set the RANGEFINDER_I2C_ADDR parameter accordingly.
+ Distance compensation for pressure and temperature are not implemented, keep in mind that ultrasonic(sonar) sensors are susceptible to temperature and pressure changes.
+ To set the minimum and maximum range the sensor can reliably measure, use the RANGEFINDER_I2C_MIN_RANGE and RANGEFINDER_I2C_MAX_RANGE parameters. Note that if rotation compensation is enabled, the effective maximum range will be reduced when the vehicle rolls or pitches. If it is impossible to measure the distance reliable, the distance value will be set to NAN (not a number).
+ To restrict the AGL range define it in your airframefile with AGL_DIST_RANGEFINDER_MAX and AGL_DIST_RANGEFINDER_MIN
+ To use this module with a Lightware Lidar SF11, SF20, SF23,SF30 VB50A, VB22A one has to add a define in module section a line like READ_MODE_SINGLE with a value of 0.
+ Most sensor datasheets give the I2C address in 7bit format. Make sure you convert this to 8bit. For example the default 7bit address of e.g. Lightware SF20/C is 0x66 one needs to use 0xCC as 8bit address in this driver.

configure.name: RANGEFINDER_I2C_PORT
configure.description: I2C device port on flightcontroller to use for this device, e.g i2c2

configure.name: RANGEFINDER_I2C_ADDR
configure.description: The I2C Slave address in 8bit of this device

configure.name: RANGEFINDER_I2C_USE_FOR_AGL
configure.description: Updates the AGL value in state,if not defined, defaults to FALSE

configure.name: RANGEFINDER_I2C_COMPENSATE_ROTATION
configure.description: Compensate AGL measurements for body rotation. Disabled by default

define.name: RANGEFINDER_I2C_USE_FILTER
define.description: If this is enabled, a median filter on the distance output, defaults to TRUE

define.name: RANGEFINDER_I2C_MEDIAN_SIZE
define.description: If median filter is enabled then set this option to filter the output more(or less), default is 7

define.name: RANGEFINDER_I2C_SCALE
define.description: Sensor scale for raw sensor output to a meter unit conversion,

define.name: RANGEFINDER_I2C_OFFSET
define.description: Sensor offset in meters, as in where one wants zero to be, default is 0.0

define.name: RANGEFINDER_I2C_MIN_RANGE
define.description: If defined, set limit to minimum value the sensor can reliably measure, default 0.25m

define.name: RANGEFINDER_I2C_MAX_RANGE
define.description: If defined, set limit to maximum value the sensor can reliably measure, default 4.0m

define.name: RANGEFINDER_I2C_SYNC_SEND
define.description: Send RAW and scaled message with each new measurement,useful for debugging sensor issues (default: FALSE)

define.name: RANGEFINDER_I2C_READ_MODE_SINGLE
define.description: Only add this define when using a Lightware Lidar SF11, SF20, SF23 or SF30
